description.narrative: Projektet syftar till att förbättra anställbarheten för långtidsarbetslös arbetskraft, särskilt ungdomar, kvinnor och personer med kort eller ingen utbildning. Projektet är en del av ett större sysselsättningsstödsprogram som genomförs av Världsbanken. Det engagerar privata arbetsförmedlare för att matcha arbetslösa med efterfrågan på arbetskraft. Projektet testar modeller för hur privata arbetsförmedlingar kan användas och utvärderar effekten av stöd till arbetslös arbetskraft.

The project aims at improving the employability of the long-term unemployed workforce, particularly youth, women, and people with short or no education or training. The project is part of a larger employment support programme implemented by the World Bank. It engages employment service providers to match unemployed with labor demand. The project tests private employment service provision models and evaluate the impact of support to the unemployed workforce.

The project overall objective is to promote job creation. Outcome indicators include percentage of beneficiaries remaining employed 12 months after the intervention, and the percentage of firms with higher number of employees 12 months after the intervention, as well as the number of job-seekers receiving counseling services. The project will do this through engaging with private employment service providers. It will then commission an impact study to check results. Following positive results, the World Bank aims to improve the effectiveness of public employment service active labor market measures, based on the successful pilots with private employment services. With an amendment request number two, the World Bank requested a 12 month no cost extension of the agreement until October 2022. This is due to delays caused primarily by COVID19 crisis. The World Bank has also updated the overall objective and the target group of the project. The target group of beneficiaries would be the hard to employ, long-term unemployed and newly unemployed due to Covid -19 pandemic (lower skilled, unemployed youth and women) The overall objective has been updated as follows: The development objective of the project is to support hard- to- employ job-seekers and newly employed job-seekers that lost their jobs due to Covid-19 pandemic, to transition into jobs through a suite of individualized and market-driven private employment services. The overall objective is updated as follows: Phase II - Economic Inclusion of Women and Improvement of Monitoring Systems aims to deliver individualized employment services to increase number of targeted women to be included in the labor market. More specifically, the pilot intervention will result in economic inclusion of 1000 women and provide evidence and practical experience to institutions. When it comes to long-term results Phase II builds on the existing work to ensure suitability of this pilot to improve analytical and delivery capacities of government institutions. Improved Social Assistance Beneficiary database will result in better targeting of unemployed, inactive and socially excluded women. Further, the intervention will result in development of guide policies that would enable governments to tailor measures for the continuous inclusion of women in labor market.

In line with the project objectives and considering the challenges of the changing labour market, the project still managed to measure meaningful results. The project is divided into two sub/projects: the first part of the project is directly implemented by the World Bank under the Bank Executed Trust Fund (RETF). This part of the project is related to business advisory services, supervision and monitoring an impact evaluation. While, the second part of the project is directly implemented by private employment agency "Kolektive under Recipient Executed Trust Fund (RETF). The activities executed within this part of the project are related to profiling and counseling of jobseekers, job inter-mediation services, on-the-job training and job placement.
When it comes to results during the reporting period project activities focused on 1) implementation of Component 2 activities (Provision of private employment services), finalizing the Impact Evaluation Report and under Component 3 Initiating the analysis of Phase II.
For easier reference expected results are listed as per component below.
Under Component 1 more specifically Call to applicants and status of application during the reporting period (October 2023 - June 2024) 3 calls were conducted with the total number of applicants amounting to 1 319 persons. However, the unexpected outcome is related to the trend of interested and eligible candidates. The trend indicates significant reduction of number of applicants and subsequently those that are eligible and received assistance. For example number of applicants during the first call within this reporting period is 864 while during the last call in this reporting period number is reduced to 115.
Counselling and Job Placement Results during the reporting period 2023 - 932 jobseekers (794 women) were counselled while 794 jobseekers (553 women) were placed in jobs. According to the Federal Employment Institute 204 jobseekers are employed and approved. In addition 31 persons have started the on-job training. In this regard the project has met the set targets however indication that the interest of jobseekers is significantly dropping over the period future similar interventions will be more challenging.
With this said, the analysis indicates that although labor supply is reducing women and long-term unemployed categories remain stagnate in statistical terms. This would be categorized as unexpected results not directly attributed to the project but to overall labor market landscape.
Further, when it comes to soft skills training for participants the private employment agency Kolektiv during the reporting period has carried out 14 soft skill training courses with an outreach to 15 620 participants and only 404 jobseekers attended trainings that are organized in person and virtually. The result in terms of the aggressive outreach is expected however it is unexpected that only 2,6 % of those who received the information actually attended.
In terms of On-the job training with the employers, similarly the trend is rather disappointing. Kolektiv cooperated with 40 employers and 38 out of these 40 were adequately corresponded to requirements of the call. Out of 781 candidates who were referred for on-the job-training only 25 (3,2%) were placed in the training with the employer. Such low number of selected candidates to be placed is not expected. According to the project team, the slow progress and unexpected results are both attributed to the employers side and the job seekers side. More specifically, on the employers side they usally postponed the hiring causing jobseekeres to lose interest, jobseekers often selected candidates from outside the proposed pool offering unattractive compensation packages. Meanwhile, on the jobseekers side, candidates often demonstrated lack of interst, not showing up or poorly completing their duties.
It would be also worth mentioning that the number of candidates would be slightly higher since over 20 unemployed low skilled women were scheduled to receive required training with a possibility for long-term employment however the the production line was postponed and recruitment was put on hold.
Regarding the Component 3 Evaluation of the impact of private services on employment outcomes as expected the publication is completed and submitted. The narrative report includes findings from the evaluation and some are listed here for reference.
"The analysis found that receiving job matching services in addition to counselling results in a six-percentage point higher likelihood of finding a formal job at the end of the program. Although slightly weaker, these differences persist in the medium term, about one year after the program's completion. Second, vulnerable groups including those with lower levels of education and youth benefit more from the matching services. For example, for jobseekers with a secondary school degree or less, job matching results in a 7.8 percentage point greater likelihood of formal employment, whereas the corresponding number for those with more some tertiary education is 2.5 percentage points. The effects of job matching are more than double for jobseekers younger than 30 than for those above the age of 30. Finally, while the effects of job matching are not statistically significant for the group of women overall, for those with children they are more than 10 percentage points. Overall, these results suggest this intervention addressed constraints faced by the most vulnerable groups in the labor market."
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
